cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Choose the Precedent
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which rule, custom, or prior decision will govern what happens now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who gets the head seat, Grandma or the birthday child? Choose which tradition we're using before I lay the places.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put two chairs there. Would that do?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For sitting, yes. Now choose which tradition decides whom I serve first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Serve them together. Except there's only one birthday pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then decide before I bring it in: elders first or birthdays first? I'll divide the pudding after the wish. Until you've chosen, nobody at those two chairs gets to call me over.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 approves B2 seating only and demands service tradition; A5 controls pudding release until B4 indivisibility is resolved by B choice.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 two chairs leads A3 first serving; B4 one pudding leads A5 first wish then division, with birthday-wish ritual introduced intelligibly.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks inclusion and B4 suggests simultaneous service, giving A genuine practical solutions to test.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 shared pudding to require a singular first moment before division, developing the same precedent choice.

specificity.evidence: A1 Grandma and birthday child, B2 chairs and B4 pudding locate the family meal clearly.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 nobody calls A over shows assumed authority over serving; it is a small flourish attached to the withheld pudding.
